services.name: Tree Pruning
services.tagline: Clean cuts that keep your tree healthy for decades.
services.shortDescription: Selective pruning to remove dead, diseased, or interfering branches. Improves tree health, shape, and safety without compromising long-term growth.
services.description:
Pruning is the difference between a tree that thrives and a tree that becomes a liability. Every cut is intentional. We remove what is dead, diseased, broken, or growing into the wrong place, and we leave what is structurally sound. Mature shade trees, young trees that need shaping for the long haul, fruit trees that have stopped producing well, and ornamental trees that have crept over the roof or driveway all benefit from a proper pruning.

Good pruning is about restraint as much as removal. Cutting too much at once stresses a tree and forces weak, fast regrowth. We make targeted cuts at the right points, respect the branch collar so the wound can close on its own, and never top a tree to reduce its size. The goal is a tree that looks better now and holds better structure for years.

Most residential pruning jobs are done in a single visit. You get a free quote before any work starts and a clean yard when we leave, with debris chipped onsite or hauled away depending on what you prefer.
process: Walk the property with you and identify which trees need work and why
Quote each tree separately so you can choose the scope and budget that fits
Climb or use a pole saw and pole pruner depending on the height and reach of the cut
Prioritize dead, diseased, broken, and crossing branches, then shape and thin as needed
Use the three-cut method on larger limbs to prevent bark tearing, and cut back to the branch collar so the tree heals cleanly
Chip or haul the debris based on your call and leave the site clean
goodFor: Mature shade trees that have not been pruned in 5 or more years
Branches overhanging the house, driveway, deck, sidewalk, or pool
Young trees that need structural pruning to set up good long-term shape
Dead, diseased, or broken wood that should come out before it falls
Crown thinning to let more light through to the lawn or garden below
Fruit and ornamental trees that have grown dense and need opening up
Trees that have outgrown their space and are crowding a fence or structure
services.seasonalNote: For most deciduous trees in southern Ontario, the dormant season from late fall through winter (roughly November to March) is the best time to prune. With the leaves down the branch structure is easy to read, and most insects and disease organisms are inactive, which lowers the risk of infection through fresh cuts. Dead, broken, or diseased wood can be taken out at any time of year and does not have to wait for dormancy. A few exceptions matter: maple, birch, and other heavy sap producers will bleed if cut in late winter or early spring, which looks messy but does not harm the tree, and they can be pruned in early summer instead if you want to avoid it. Spring-flowering trees like lilac, magnolia, and crabapple are best pruned right after they finish blooming, since they set next year's buds the previous summer. Oaks are the strict one: to reduce the risk of oak wilt, oaks should not be pruned during the growing season, so we keep oak work to the dormant window (roughly November through March) unless a branch is broken and has to be dealt with for safety.

services.name: Limb Removal
services.tagline: Hanging, broken, or in the way? Down it comes.
services.shortDescription: Removal of individual large limbs that are dead, broken, hanging, or interfering with structures. The step up from light pruning when a single limb is the problem.
services.description:
Sometimes a tree is fundamentally healthy but one or two limbs have become a problem. A branch left hanging after a storm, a limb growing onto the roof or into the lines, a heavy dead leader that is shedding wood over the driveway. Taking out those specific limbs is less involved than taking down a whole tree, and it solves the immediate hazard without removing a tree that is otherwise fine.

This is targeted, careful work. For limbs over a structure we set rope and a lower line and bring the wood down in controlled sections, so nothing drops where it should not. The final cut is made clean at the branch collar so the tree can close the wound and heal properly. A limb that is torn off or cut badly leaves an open wound that invites decay, which is exactly what good removal avoids.

A quick safety note. If a limb is touching or near a power line, leave it alone and call your utility. The same goes for limbs that are under tension or partly suspended in the canopy. Those are dangerous to approach, so let us assess them rather than risk it yourself. Most limb removals are a same-day or next-evening job once we have looked at it.
process: Look at the limb, the tree, and what is underneath, then identify safe rigging points
Confirm nothing is in or near a power line before any cutting starts
Set rope and a lower line for any limb hanging over a structure or target
Section the limb from the tip back so the wood stays under control the whole way down
Make a final clean cut at the branch collar so the tree can heal and resist decay
Chip or haul the wood, then clean up the site so the yard is left tidy
goodFor: Storm-damaged, broken, or hanging limbs (often called widow-makers when suspended in the canopy)
Dead leader branches and deadwood that are dropping pieces below
Limbs over the roof, garage, deck, fence, pool, or driveway
A single problem limb on an otherwise healthy tree
Branches rubbing against the house, a wall, or another structure
Limbs that have developed a crack or a weak V-shaped union and could fail
Low or awkward branches blocking access, a path, or a sightline
services.seasonalNote: Dead, broken, hanging, and storm-damaged limbs can be removed at any time of year. You do not have to wait for the dormant season when a limb is a hazard, since leaving a cracked or suspended branch in the canopy is the bigger risk. The one species to flag is oak. To reduce the risk of oak wilt, oaks should not be pruned or wounded during the growing season, so for non-urgent oak limb work we schedule it for the dormant window (roughly November through March). If an oak limb breaks in a storm during the warm months and has to come down for safety, that is the recognized exception, and the fresh wound can be treated to make it less attractive to the sap beetles that spread the disease. After a storm, the safest move is to clear small fallen branches from the ground, photograph the damage for your insurance, stay well clear of anything near a power line or under tension, and let us handle the limbs that are up in the tree.

services.name: Full Tree Removal
services.shortDescription: Full tree removal is in the launch plan but not yet offered. Pruning and limb work first, full removals will be added once the rig and crew are scaled for it.
services.description:
Full tree removal requires bucket-truck access (for street trees) or experienced ground crew with rigging gear (for backyard removals). Both are in the plan. For now, we focus on pruning and limb removal jobs that can be done safely with current tools and experience.

If you need a full tree taken down soon, send a photo of the tree and we will tell you who to call.
